reviewed_sources.finding: M grammar has no trailing OBJECT. Only initial user during OM-controlled upgrade with nonzero upgrade_mode and application_name=OM. Produces system-object rollback script files.
General mode adds OBJECT but gives the same prerequisites; no output lifecycle details. Not reused as M grammar.
SIGHUP upgrade parameter: 0 normal, 1 inplace, 2 grey. Document warns manual changes can break upgrade/rollback and have unpredictable effects outside upgrades.

auto_script invokes rollback-script generation, is not recommended for ordinary users, and is stage/strategy dependent. Examples mention cleaning temporary files but do not identify the SQL command's output paths, ownership, contents or safe standalone cleanup. Upgrade tool logs are not the rollback-script artifact contract.

local_checks: Read complete M command chapter and rendered physical page 2211, including syntax diagram

Inspected exact upgrade parameter and tool sections; verified chapter hashes and same parent PDF
missing_contract: Actual supported OM upgrade stage and external fixture provider; not merely matching two GUC strings
Initial-user identity verification without treating SYSADMIN as equivalent
Generated rollback file locations/naming, ownership and isolation boundary
Expected artifact contents or format and deterministic success/failure oracle
Stage-aware recovery/cleanup ownership, including partial failure; no guessed rm or upgrade rollback command
rejected_shortcuts: Do not SET upgrade_mode or run gs_upgradectl just to obtain a passing smoke test
Do not use an unrelated CREATE TABLE, SELECT 1, SHOW or arbitrary ROLLBACK as fake fixture lifecycle
Do not assume general-mode OBJECT suffix applies to M
Do not mark an arbitrary rejected execution as target-negative verification
Do not rename missing semantics as unsupported or accept an empty generated suite
required_input: An authoritative OM integration/test-fixture specification for this SQL command, including prerequisite stage, output artifacts and lifecycle ownership. Additional database execution authorization is NOT requested or implied.
